**SFK 2000 Sarajevo** ([Bosnian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnian_language "Bosnian language"): ŽFK 2000 Sarajevo) is a women's professional football club from the city of [Sarajevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarajevo "Sarajevo") that is situated in [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina"). The club competes in the highest level of women's football in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the [Bosnia and Herzegovina Women's Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_Women's_Premier_League "Bosnia and Herzegovina Women's Premier League"). The club was established in June 2000; the name was chosen from a lower-tier men's football club which is now defunct.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SFK_2000#cite_note-1)
Following its foundation, the club quickly won the national championship, and has subsequently dominated women's football in the country, winning 24 consecutive titles so far. The club has participated in the [UEFA Women's Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Women's_Cup "UEFA Women's Cup") from 2003 onwards and has reached the final rounds four times. In the [2009–10 UEFA Women's Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Women's_Champions_League "2009–10 UEFA Women's Champions League"), when the competition was rebranded and reorganized, the side started in the round of 32 but lost to Russia's [Zvezda 2005 Perm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zvezda_2005_Perm "Zvezda 2005 Perm") 8–0 on aggregate. In the next two years the team had to go through the qualifying phase, failing both times, but in the [2012–13 UEFA Women's Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_UEFA_Women's_Champions_League "2012–13 UEFA Women's Champions League") they managed to qualify after hosting the qualifying phase in Sarajevo and defeating two clubs which played the [round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_UEFA_Women's_Champions_League#Round_of_32 "2011–12 UEFA Women's Champions League") of the previous season of the Women's champions league.
The club advanced to the [round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Women's_Champions_League#Round_of_32 "2018–19 UEFA Women's Champions League") once again, this time in the [2018–19 UEFA Women's Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Women's_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Women's Champions League") season, but got eliminated by [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C._Women "Chelsea F.C. Women") 11–0 on aggregate.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SFK_2000#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SFK_2000#cite_note-3)
On 4 July 2015, SFK 2000 signed an agreement on long-term cooperation with Bosnian men's football club [FK Sarajevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FK_Sarajevo "FK Sarajevo"), by which SFK 2000 assumed the latter's maroon and white colors, club logo and kit.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SFK_2000#cite_note-4) FK Sarajevo board members entered the SFK 2000 board, by which the two clubs became to _de facto_ function as one.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SFK_2000#cite_note-5)
